question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout once the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The code shape is focused and privacy-protective, but disabling existing opt-ins and adding a Play Data Safety release lane are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Resolve conflicts and confirm rollout
options.body: Rebase the PR, preserve current Android settings/release behavior, then merge after maintainer approval of the reset, disclosure copy, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy alignment.

options.title: Adjust disclosure or rollout first
options.body: Change the dialog wording, placement, CSV, or release sequencing if Play review or maintainer privacy expectations require a different shape.

options.title: Hold the PR
options.body: Keep the branch paused if the external Play Console or privacy-policy materials are not ready to ship with the code.

recommendation.title: Resolve conflicts and confirm rollout
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, preserve current Android settings/release behavior, then merge after maintainer approval of the reset, disclosure copy, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy alignment.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner because the remaining blocker is Android release/privacy rollout approval plus conflict refresh across recently changed Android settings surfaces.
